So this is just material that has been recopied and disclosed again, presented again, and now I have to deal with it all. So that's what I wanted to say. Thank you for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, I understood you perfectly. I would like to know whether the parties want to raise other questions, starting with Mr. Stamp, do you have anything else to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There is one issue. The Defence in the pre-trial brief filing raised the Defence of alibi for a particular period in the indictment. And while we are grateful for that may I just take the opportunity to remind them, because this matter will become the matter of proceedings very shortly, to remind them that the rules provide that it is not sufficient just to raise the issue of alibi but the Defence ought to submit the places where he was supposed to have been at the relevant time, as well as the witnesses and the documents that will go to substantiate the alibi. So I place our concern about that on the record and indicate that we will take appropriate steps if that is not done in due course. And I just -- may I just say by way of reminder, I don't know if it's something that the Court had considered dealing with, there is another outstanding motion, I think, before the Court. It is not filed by any party to this case, it was filed by counsel in another proceeding asking for access to our confidential matter in this case. I raise it because earlier on Your Honour had referred to outstanding motions and did not mention this one so I just raise it in case it was an oversight there. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I will give you the floor in a minute but regarding the Defence of alibi, as you know, under the rules, it is a possibility stated for but this is no obligation. The Defence can at any time, but also during the pre-trial phase, say to the Prosecution that it intends to raise a defence of alibi for specific reasons. The accusation -- the Prosecution was informed and therefore asked for further information of the Defence, whether, for instance, the Accused was not in a specific place, and this should be provided by way of documents or witness names. This is what the Prosecution would like to know. I therefore turn to the Defence for an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we could have done this later on. It doesn't say strictly in the rules that this must be stated in our response to the pre-trial brief by the Prosecutor. But we wanted our conduct to be proper and to announce this straight away and I can say directly here and now, or rather I can give you a piece of information here and now, and that is that we have medical documents from which you can see that for the wounds to the head and the eye at the front where he was in command that he was treated at the hospital in Belgrade and we have medical records and records that state that quite clearly. Now, other things concerning that problem, even -- I don't think that it is our duty to deal with all these matters, because that would enter into the realm of questions that the Defence will deal with in the Defence case and we would uncover our steps if we were to do so but we have absolute evidence that at that time the person was in Belgrade undergoing medical treatment and that they were in fact in hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I take note of what you have just said. However, what you just cited is very relevant. You are free to prove the defence of alibi at any time. You don't have to do so right now. You can wait until you present the Defence case. You are free to do so. However, however, should it be established on the basis of the elements you have that your client at the relevant time in the indictment did not exert his command responsibility because he was in a hospital, this may prompt the Prosecution to withdraw that count or change it because it is obvious in international law and also in criminal law that somebody who does not exert a command is replaced by somebody else, and if that person was not there at the specific point in time obviously he was replaced by somebody, all the more so since he had been admitted into hospital. There may be some dispute, I don't know what your evidence is, but if you do have such evidence, you are free to disclose it to the Prosecution so that the Prosecution may look into the indictment and draw specific conclusions, but you know the trial has to be expeditious, your client is in detention, and if you do have evidence likely to be exculpatory, why should you wait? Why not provide them straight away to the Prosecution? It's up to you. I, as the Pre-Trial Judge, cannot rule one way or another. I am only here as a referee. I am not here to tell you what to do but it is my duty to tell you that there are provisions in the indictment that the Prosecution can at any time amend the indictment but it can only do so if certain evidence is provided by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your words of warning. I know that full well. But I do not wish to enter into the details of all this because there are a number of problems we have to overcome, not only whether he was the commander at that time but other things as well. So I have presented this information before you as the basic reason for which we are asking what we are asking in our motion, in our pre-trial brief. If you wish to hear more details, I can give them to the Prosecution, but at this point in time I think it is sufficient that we have understood each other. I will take note of your guidelines and in due course I will present the case to the Prosecution and the Court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We are close to the end of the hearing. To sum up, I can see that there are still translation problems, some documents are not translated yet, so I do urge the Registrar and the registry to make sure that the documents be translated. I note that the Prosecution can, on this very day, provide the documents that have been translated, even possibly documents related to witnesses 42, 56, and 127. I believe I also noted that all parties wanted to -- the two parties wanted to meet straight after the hearing in order to try to solve some problems. Equally I note that the Accused said that he had no health problems. This is being noted. Immediately after the hearing, I will put the issue of the computer to the Registrar. Indeed, I think that is something that has to be clarified. Regarding the defence of alibi and Rule 67, we have had some exchanges. It is up to the Defence to do what they feel they have to do. In this respect, I'm not supposed to intervene. Still, I did try to guide the Defence. As I indicated at the beginning of the hearing, I am going to finalise my report to be sent to my colleagues by the end of the week. I believe this case should start soon. The Prosecution has finished its work regarding the pre-trial brief, the exhibit, and the witness list. Even if it could have been better, a lot has been done by the Prosecution compared to what was done in other cases. Therefore, there is no objective reason why we should postpone any further, and a date for the commencement of the trial should be found by the committee in charge of it. I mean, if I was free to start, I could start in two weeks' time but since I am scheduled to hear another case, I cannot make this promise to you. You will have other judges hearing the case and they will be appointed by the president of the Tribunal. This being so, I do hope that we will not meet again. Of course, it would be lovely to see you but this case has to move ahead. I wish you all the best in this case. I'm going to send my report to my colleagues in a very few days' time. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
